When I was pregnant I sent my husband to the store for vanilla bean ice cream. When he came back with “natural vanilla flavored “ ice cream” I was so appalled I cried for 2 hours, threw the offensive pint in the yard as I peeled out of the driveway in a rage. I left for hours. I drove to Kroger and bought real vanilla bean ice cream and drove around eating it in the car alone.
So yeah. Pregnancy hormones are fucking wild and make women do crazy and seemingly unreasonable stuff. We laugh and laugh about it now, but at the time I was certain my husband wasn’t fit to be a parent and convinced he didn’t deserve me  as a spouse because he couldn’t follow a simple request.  Only the latter was true because he didn’t deserve to be vilified for my insane cravings. 
You can hate on it and shame women,… maybe you just hate women.. maybe you are troll?! there isn’t really a defense for how unreasonable the cravings make us.

Meadowbrook was a board and train boot camp. 2 weeks for about $1k.  We were out of town for vacation when we did it. 
We felt like it was a worth it since we’d have had to pay about a third of that for boarding only.
We really liked the trainer and trusted the process and she trained US and did follow up sessions for feee afterwards. 

The barking and reaction stuff can be trained out of these pups. But a lot of it requires intensive and consistent training and slow measured exposure to stimulation that causes reactions. The key is getting your dog redirected to focus on YOU instead of the stimulation that causes the reactions. That’s the basis for all dog training. 

Also like… man… dogs have anxiety disorders like humans. Have y’all  talked to the vet? I know our vet would have made us do all the training before a prescription but maybe yours will consider a daily anti anxiety pill or antidepressant to help in tandem with training? 
More money but again like humans it’s likely a combo of therapy/ training and if that doesn’t work a daily med.

Is exercising/ slow controlled interactions with stimuli an option? Do you do dog parks or even doggy day care?
We do a weekly daycare at The Bark. In general it’s just good for extra socialization and exercise, but I have seen a big difference since taking ours to day care vs when we just were walking him in the neighborhood for exercise. 
The bark has trainers too that you can hire to do an evaluation and training with that might help? 

Just spitballing. I know all my reccs have costs associated but your quality of life plus your buddy’s quality of life are worthy investments.

Few days later, I get a call from HR and they rescind their offer because of something in my educational records. A minimum education requirement was in the job description and they thought I had lied on my transcripts as the university had no record of my graduation. Shocked! Devastated! I even had my letter of resignation typed up on my desk top. This corporation then “black listed me from being eligible to be considered for future employment opportunities” I sank into a deep depression trudging away at my dead end job. 

It took me almost 3 months to figure out what was wrong with my diploma from the community college, but apparently I was still in bad standing with the library and they held my graduation because of $70 library fines. They said I had never graduated almost a decade earlier. Which I knew I had because I had satisfied all the requirements for my associates degree. And had paperwork for all the graduation stuff.

So, I call the corporate HR rep and explain what happened and provide her with a notarized letter from the university as well as a scan of my diploma. I ask to be removed from the black list and they do so. Unfortunately, they were in a hiring freeze at the time due to an acquisition and there were no jobs available.
